item.text: {"text":"SASRec combines item and absolute positional embeddings, so compacting a history after deletion changes both content and surviving items’ positions. Its fixed history window also introduces truncation effects. ([SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781)) Recommended controls, inferred from this architecture: compare compact deletion against removal with surviving position IDs preserved; use content replacement at fixed positions and sequence length; shift position IDs while retaining identical content; compare against random deletions matched on count and recency. Freeze the original visible window before perturbation so deletion cannot pull older interactions into view; evaluate backfilling separately. Keep target, candidate set, and readout rule fixed, explicitly handling deletion of the final interaction. Padding is not a neutral replacement when it changes attention masks. These contrasts diagnose confounds rather than guarantee an additive causal decomposition.\n\nFaithfulness asks whether a perturbation changes the fitted model’s specified prediction. On training prefixes, report paired target-score, margin, or rank changes as training-prefix sensitivity; these do not establish next-item generalization or real-world preference effects. Fix the target before deletion, distinguish original-model recommendations from observed next items, disable dropout, and summarize uncertainty across users. Perturbation studies warn that out-of-distribution inputs can distort faithfulness measurements; random-removal baselines help, while retraining evaluates an adapted model and answers a different question. ([ROAR](https://research.google/pubs/evaluating-feature-importance-estimates/), [Recursive ROAR](https://mcgill-nlp.github.io/publications/nlp_recursive_roar/)) For this task, report generalization separately through the unchanged held-out validation protocol: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, seed 42, macro HR@10 across all four categories. Training-prefix diagnostics may motivate changes; validation HR@10 selects them. Keep test labels unavailable throughout search."}
